architecture_decisions: API-first modular monolith; no browser frontend in release 0.1.0.
Canonical Pydantic hierarchy preserves raw evidence, normalized text, coordinates, provenance, and verification history.
Native PDF text is attempted before raster OCR; model providers are adapter ports.
Local immutable artifact storage is the development default; PostgreSQL/S3/Redis remain ports for production deployment.
OCR-required regions use bounded crop/preprocess variants; selected retry geometry is mapped back to rendered page pixels.
Mixed PDF pages preserve native text and append OCR blocks for embedded image regions.
Word geometry is emitted when a backend supplies word boxes; confidence scales are never cross-compared without calibration.
Phase-specific ingestion classifies every PDF page independently and preserves native evidence before bounded raster rendering.
PDF/image readers are provider adapters behind PdfExtractor/PageRenderer; application ingestion depends on ArtifactStore rather than a concrete storage implementation.
Raster inspection uses signature-aware Pillow decoding, EXIF correction, metadata-only PDF image-region discovery, and configured resource limits.
Phase 4 preprocessing is immutable, profile-driven, bounded, and records per-step artifact/mapping provenance; tiny-text escalation is explicit and verification-required.
Phase 5 layout is provider-neutral and pre-OCR: normalized geometry, stable taxonomy, explicit route hints, confidence gates, and spatial RTL/LTR reading order are preserved before OCR invocation.

Phase 6 routes printed OCR, handwriting, tables, and mixed forms through separate provider ports; raw candidates, runtime warnings, structured cells, verification history, and source-derived line crops remain auditable.
Phase 11 adds retention governance, traversal-safe authenticated deletion, private export staging, review audit records, bounded upload pixels, and content-redacting logs.

Phase 12 adds validated device/model lifecycle settings, bounded metrics, optional tracing, capability-aware readiness, page checkpoints, DPI/resource profiling, and non-root model-weight-free containers.
assumptions: Deployments install optional OCR/layout/HTR backends and model weights separately.
The current environment may not have heavyweight dependencies; unavailable integrations must be reported as NOT_RUN, not simulated.
risks: Backend confidence scales require per-backend calibration.
High-DPI/tiny-text processing requires strict resource limits.
Complex reading order for mixed RTL/multi-column pages is heuristic without a deployed layout model.
Compressed PDFs may still require operational CPU/time quotas beyond page/pixel limits; processing timeout enforcement remains an application-worker concern.
Multipage raster containers and advanced capture-quality signals are not yet expanded in ingestion.

The configurable HTR adapter and table-cell adapter are present, but their production runtimes and model weights are not installed in the current environment; capability checks fail closed and require review.
The local worker persists page checkpoints but does not reclaim queued work after process restart; a durable shared queue is required for multi-instance recovery.

task_03_handwriting_htr.objective: Configurable provider-neutral handwriting recognition with fail-closed capability handling and provenance-preserving routing
decisions: Transformers HTR is a lazy optional adapter selected by configurable model ID or local path; provider objects do not leak into canonical domain models.
The base installation does not import Torch or Transformers and standard tests never download model weights.
Local-files-only is the default and trust_remote_code is disabled by default; enabling remote access or remote code is an explicit deployment decision.
The adapter reports configured language and script metadata only; it makes no Persian or Arabic handwriting capability claim without a validated configured model and benchmark.

Unavailable or failed HTR is surfaced through typed errors and review flags. Optional printed OCR fallback is explicitly labeled as fallback and cannot be exported as verified handwriting ground truth.
HTR confidence remains None with an explicit uncalibrated confidence scale when the configured model does not provide a calibrated score.
